pergunta: Remind me which installment limit we talked about last time?
resposta:
Our last conversation (4 Nov 2026) was about splitting a sale with the Crediário. The limit is up to 48 installments on a credit card [1][5].

pergunta: And who pays the interest?
resposta:
The cardholder, meaning your customer, pays the interest on Crediário installments [1][3].

- The maximum term and the interest rate vary by card issuer.
- On the card machine, the customer can see the interest in a simulation (credit > crediário). The customer can also print a receipt of the simulation to check the interest and the final purchase amount [2].
- You receive the sale in a single payment within 2 business days after the transaction is captured, whatever the number of installments. The discount fee is subtracted from the original amount [5].

pergunta: E os juros, quem define?
resposta:
Quem define os juros do parcelamento no Crediário é o emissor do cartão. A taxa de juros e o prazo máximo variam de acordo com o emissor [3][4]. O emissor também define o limite de parcelas, conforme as políticas de crédito dele [1].

Para ver as condições antes de fechar a venda, faça a simulação na maquininha. Insira o cartão e o valor e escolha crédito > crediário. Se a maquininha tiver bobina, dá para imprimir o comprovante da simulação. A simulação serve só para consulta e fica sujeita à análise de crédito. pergunta: How does receivables advance (antecipação) work with Getnet?
resposta:
Receivables advance (antecipação de vendas) lets you receive the value of your credit-card sales early, for both lump-sum and installment sales, instead of waiting for the normal settlement period [6].

- **Timing:** You can advance a sale's schedule from D+1 (one business day after the sale). It stays available until D-3 (three business days before it would settle) [7].
- **Example:** A sale made on 04/03 can be advanced from 05/03. If it would normally be credited on 03/04, you can advance it until 31/03 [9].
- **Card brands:** Some enabled brands can't be advanced through Getnet. For those, you have to go through the brand's own operator [7].
- **Automatic advance:** This is a condition for the exemption on the "Receba Conforme suas Vendas" plan. It goes through credit approval, and Getnet assesses each contract individually [3].
- **E-commerce:** Advances on e-commerce sales are blocked for 6 months. Physical-store sales can still be advanced normally [5].
- **Collateral (gravame):** If your receivables are collateral for a loan, they go to the lender. With Getnet's loan, your sales from Getnet and other acquirers are paid into your Get Conta, up to the outstanding loan balance [1][2].
